notes:
POC summary and outcome (stalled -> closed-lost to competitor).

Context: Mosaic is building a latencysensitive in-store conversational assistant used on kiosks and mobile. Requirement: p95 generation latency <= 300ms for short chat replies (<= 60 tokens) and stable token streaming for voice-to-text path. Heavy concurrency during store hours (peak 200 concurrent sessions per region).

What we ran: 2-week Dedicated POC in us-west-2 on g5x2 equivalent, serving a trimmed base-llama variant. Workload: conversational turns + real-time reranking of product suggestions. Traffic profile supplied by Mosaic (timeline + synthetic replay).

Engineering notes / findings:
- Observed p95 steady ~1.6-2.2s on default Dedicated config; spikes to 3.8s under burst. Target is 0.3s.
- Streaming saw choppy SSE with 80ms+ gaps between chunks; voice pipeline reported audible stutter.
- Root cause (R&D hypothesis): batching and kernel choices tuned for throughput on longer sequences; KV cache warmup behavior caused first-token tail latency.
- SE attempts: smaller batch caps, lowered inter-request coalescing, adjusted warmup prefill. Gains: p95 improved to ~1.1s but still above SLO.
- Caching suggestion (prefix caching) reduced tail for repeat prompts but did not address cold-starts and new session churn.
- Memory/throughput tradeoff: further reductions required moving to higher-clock GPUs (costly) or model quantization (risk to quality).

Customer reactions:
- "We need sub-300ms for live kiosks — anything above that impacts perceived snappiness and adoption," product VP said on 2026-01-15 call (ff-20260115-34Xq).
- Infra lead: accepted tradeoffs but balked at doubling committed spend for marginal latency gains.

Commercial outcome:
- Mosaic began parallel eval with FastPathAI (their engineered streaming runtime) in late Jan. FastPathAI demonstrated 240-320ms p95 under same replay using their lightweight streaming path.
- Internal procurement paused due to budget reforecast for FY26; no internal champion to push higher commit.
- Decision: Mosaic disqualified Redwood Dedicated for kiosk use-case for now; marked as lost to competitor for this workload. They may revisit for non-real-time reranking/analytics functions.

Follow-ups / artifacts:
- POC bench results in Drive (linked).
- Support tickets logged for streaming anomalies (SUP-3819, SUP-4021) with trace dumps attached.
- SE notes: suggested private deployment + specialized kernel scheduling as long-term path — customer declined given timeline and cost.

Sales notes / next steps:
- Close opportunity as lost-to-competitor with technical root cause documented.
- Keep trial data for Optimize team to analyze potential runtime improvements.
- Re-engagement plan: Q3 check-in about lower-cost inference options and non-realtime products (embeddings, nightly rerank).

Misc: call transcripts, product quotes, and perf graphs saved in Drive.
